summary: Candidate bab33e2e1c26450edc7661eb4de484af3d331740 adds valid tests for optional returned-hidden-state slicing but does not reproduce or explain ordinary Kimi-K3 generated-text leakage. Independent checks show the cited offset correction is already an ancestor of official v0.5.17 and that ordinary requests with return_hidden_states=False bypass the tested response slicer. The useful candidate tests are preserved and an ordinary-generation boundary is added; no production source change is justified.

tests.what_was_measured: Exact candidate bab33e2e1c26450edc7661eb4de484af3d331740: 9 tests and 2 subtests pass, confirming its returned-hidden-state regressions are internally valid.
The upstream PR #30177 implementation commit is contained in the official v0.5.17 tag, contradicting the candidate's causal chronology.

tests.what_was_measured: Mechanism-level failing-before evidence: the retained regression observed offset 3 instead of 8. The rollback was restored immediately; because official v0.5.17 already has the corrected order, this is not evidence reproducing the reported v0.5.17 symptom.
10 tests and 2 subtests pass, including preserved candidate coverage and the added ordinary-generation boundary that commits a sampled token without invoking hidden-state response slicing.

On the assigned AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950, the retained helper advanced from offset 0 to 8 and selected [[20], [21], [22]] for the requesting request. This qualifies only the optional hidden-state response helper.

remaining_limitations: Kimi-K3 weights were unavailable, so Kimi-K3 generation and reasoning semantics were not reproduced.
The report used tensor parallelism across eight NVIDIA B300 GPUs; this environment provides one AMD gfx950 GPU.
No deterministic reproducer or request corpus was supplied for the intermittent symptom, so repeated randomized scheduling cannot establish equivalence to the report.
No concurrent HTTP, eight-way tensor-parallel, B300, or production-load claim is made.
The tiny deterministic Llama fixture was inspected but not treated as Kimi-K3 evidence because it only qualifies transport and engine execution.

No failing-before/passing-after production regression exists because the investigated candidate mechanism is already fixed in v0.5.17 and is bypassed by ordinary requests; fabricating a source correction would be speculative.
